https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/03/misk.text: Menü Kereső Nem fogják engedni senkinek, hogy kórházban ragadt csecsemőket ringasson az utcáról beesve Belföld Pintér Luca Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Az országban Miskolc az egyik gócpont, ahol kiemelkedően sok kórházban ragadt gyerek van. Múlt héten összesen 32 csecsemőt gondoztak a város egyik kórházában, de a szám napról napra változik, hangzik el abban a videóban, amit Kátai-Németh Vilmos Facebook-oldalán osztottak meg. A szociális és családügyi miniszter Hegedűs Zsolt egészségügyi miniszterrel, Buga László fekvőbeteg-ellátásért felelős államtitkárral és Gyurkó Szilvia gyermekjogi és gyermekvédelmi államtitkárral múlt pénteken látogatta meg az egyik miskolci kórházat azért, hogy minél több információt szerezzenek arról, hogyan lehet lerövidíteni a csecsemők kórházi tartózkodását. Országos szinten ugyanis több mint 320 gyerek rekedt egészségügyi intézményekben, akik átlagosan több mint 105 napot töltenek bent. Kátai-Németh Vilmos ezért célvizsgálatot rendelt el az egyedi sorsrendezésük érdekében. Gyurkó Szilvia szerint a minisztérium mindent megtesz azért, hogy ez a helyzet megoldódjon. „Addig is, amíg hatékony lépéseket tudnak tenni, szükség van arra, hogy azok, akik önkéntesként, civilként teljesítik azokat a feltételeket, és megtanulják, hogyan tudnak jól segíteni ezeknek a babáknak, be tudjanak kerülni ezekbe az intézményekbe” – mondta az államtitkár. Ezeknek az önkénteseknek higiéniai oktatáson, foglalkozás-egészségügyi vizsgálaton és több más szűrőn kell átesniük ahhoz, hogy egyáltalán bekerülhessenek az egészségügyi intézményekbe, vagyis az utcáról beesve senki nem állhat be csecsemőket ringatni. „Aki segíteni szeretne ezeknek a gyerekeknek, előbb tájékozódjon arról, hogy mely civil szervezetek kaptak felhatalmazást arra, hogy önkénteseik révén részt vehessenek a programban” – hangsúlyozta Gyurkó. Nem véletlenül utalt erre az államtitkár. Már több mint húszezer tagja van annak a csoportnak, amelyik múlt héten önkénteseket kezdett toborozni a kórházakban ragadt csecsemők mellé. A történet ott indult, hogy Balogh Tamás influenszer bő egy hete csodálkozott rá arra a szomorú tényre, ami évtizedek óta feszíti a kórházi dolgozókat: több száz gyerek él kórházakban úgy, hogy többségüknek már egyáltalán nincs szüksége egészségügyi ellátásra. Balogh a Kistarcsai Flór Ferenc Kórházban járt, ahol akkor éppen – bejegyzése szerint – 11 csecsemőt gondoztak a kórházi dolgozók. Miután a férfi megosztotta a történetet, több százan jelentkeztek az intézménynél is, hogy csecsemőket simogassanak. A kórház végül közleményben próbálta hárítani a rohamot, mondván már van önkéntes programjuk, és egyáltalán nem keresnek új önkénteseket. „A jó szándék fontos. Egy kórházban fekvő csecsemő mellett azonban ez önmagában nem elég” – írta a kezdeményezéssel szinte egy időben a szociális és családügyi miniszter, miután több kórházi önkéntesi tapasztalattal rendelkező civil szervezettel egyeztetett. A miniszter szerint is kiemelten fontos, hogy az önkéntesek hogyan közelednek ezekhez a betegekhez vagy korai traumát átélt gyerekekhez. „Az önkéntesnek tudnia kell, hogyan emelhet fel biztonságosan egy kisbabát, miként igazodjon az infúzióhoz vagy a tápszondához, milyen változásoknál kell azonnal ápolót hívnia, hogyan ismerje fel a hospitalizáció és a trauma jeleit, és miként kapcsolódjon a gyermekhez úgy, hogy biztonságot adjon, ne újabb bizonytalanságot” – írta. A civil szervezetekkel együttműködve dolgozták ki a képzési és szervezeti minimumokat, amelyek szükségesek ahhoz, hogy a kórházak biztonsággal fogadhassák az önkénteseket, jelenlétük pedig valódi segítséget jelentsen a gyermekeknek és az ott dolgozóknak. https://www.dw.com/en/germany-interior-m.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IVCw An explosive-laden drone found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport Image: Axel Schmidt/REUTERS Advertisement Germany 's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt on Sunday warned that hybrid warfare attacks had become a daily threat to the country. "We're not at war, but we are the daily target of hybrid warfare," Dobrindt told the newspaper Bild am Sonntag following the discovery of a drone carrying explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport. "Espionage, sabotage, cyberattacks, or covert operations by foreign powers aimed at destabilizing Germany or inflicting direct harm are a constant reality," Dobrindt said. He also noted that the country is stepping up research into drones to address new security threats . A new drone security research center will be established later in August at a German Aerospace Center (DLR) test airport in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt , Dobrindt said. Drone warfare: German startup draws on Ukraine's experience To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Drones spotted above military base in west Germany On Saturday, Germany 's armed forces confirmed that two drones had been spotted late on Thursday over a German military base in Mechernich in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia near the Belgian border. The drones were detected at around 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) over the Bundeswehr base, a German armed forces spokesperson said. German media reported that the base hosts personnel responsible for the maintenance of US Patriot air defense systems, which play a key role in defending Ukraine against Russian aerial attacks. Drone incident at Leipzig airport The sighting in Mechernich comes just two days after the discovery of a drone carrying explosives a Ukrainian transport plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport, an incident Dobrindt called a "hybrid attack scenario." While German government officials have refrained from publicly blaming any foreign country over the Leipzig incident, some lawmakers have pointed fingers at Russia , which has been at war with Ukraine since ​its full-scale invasion of the country in 2022. On Friday, the Russian Embassy in Berlin dismissed the Leipzig event as a "fabricated provocation" and said Russia was once more being accused of hostile actions "without the slightest evidence being presented." https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq5y.text: Image source, Getty Images By Lauren Turner Published 15 September 2026 All flights have been suspended from one of Italy's busiest airports because of volcanic ash released from nearby Mount Etna. It is the second time in recent months that Catania International Airport, on the island of Sicily, has stopped flights due to emissions from Etna, which is Europe's tallest active volcano and erupts frequently. Airport officials said arrivals and departures, which were first halted on Monday, would be suspended until 22:00 (20:00 GMT) on Tuesday. Ongoing activity at Etna prompted the INGV Etneo Observatory to issue a red aviation alert on Monday. In a statement on its website on Tuesday, Catania - Italy's fifth-busiest airport by passenger traffic - said further updates would follow. It also advised passengers due to fly from Catania to check with their airline for updates before travelling to the airport. Catania, which usually serves about 12 million passengers each year, was closed for almost a week during the peak summer season last month because of volcanic activity. There have been calls for the airport to shut and other facilities in Sicily to be expanded because of its proximity to Etna. The volcano, which stands at 3,324 metres (10,906ft), is about 40km (25 miles) away from the airport. Despite air traffic disruption, August's eruption drew large crowds of onlookers to Etna's lava flows. About 1.5 million people visit Etna every year. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: Footage shows attacked French mayor in occupied West Bank West Bank Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in West Bank French mayor and archbishop also attacked during violent attempt to stop Palestinians harvesting olives Emma Graham-Harrison in Taybeh Sat 17 Oct 2026 14.57 EDT First published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 14.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Israeli settler militants have attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of Cambrai in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank , injuring three people and damaging a car, in the latest violent attempt to prevent Palestinians from harvesting olives on their own land. Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was wearing his red, white and blue sash of office and attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates when he was assaulted and knocked to the ground on Saturday. The masked militant shouted “Vive la France” as he launched the attack, a witness said. Badoux’s wife, and Vincent Dollmann, archbishop of Cambrai, were also threatened by the group of seven men, some armed with clubs. The group had joined the olive harvest on lands belonging to the Christian town of Taybeh, along with the French consul general in Jerusalem, his wife and other diplomats, and the Belgian and Polish consuls. Settlers first attacked a group working on the lower slopes of hills near Taybeh. As well as stealing olives, they kicked, abused and assaulted a Palestinian woman in her seventies and beat a man so badly he needed six stitches for a head injury. Then they approached the diplomats and Badoux, who was in Taybeh for the launch of a twinning agreement with his town in northern France. During the attack, the militants smashed the window of an armoured car belonging to the Belgian mission. View image in fullscreen The smashed window of mayor Badoux’s car. Photograph: Emma Graham-Harrison/The Guardian Maxime Prévot, Belgium’s deputy prime minister and minister of foreign affairs, condemned the violence against Palestinians, foreign diplomats and journalists, and said his country would continue to push for European Union sanctions on settlers. “Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack,” he said. “This violence cannot be separated from Israel’s illegal settlement policy … The occupation of the Palestinian territory must end.” Palestinian residents of Taybeh have lived with years of escalating attacks from Israeli militants, but settlers had never targeted foreign diplomats there, said Father Bashar Fawadleh, the town’s parish priest. “What happened today is not an isolated incident. It represents a deeply disturbing escalation in settler violence,” Fawadleh said. Since the start of the annual olive harvest in late September, Israeli militants have used violence to stop Palestinians bringing in a crop that is economically and culturally vital to their communities. Since 27 September, settlers have launched more than 170 attacks, Israeli rights group Yesh Din said. They killed at least four people, injured more than 100 and damaged thousands of trees, according to Palestinian authorities. Even the presence of Israeli activists, diplomats, senior clergy and journalists no longer serves as a deterrence to extreme violence. “If such violence can take place before international witnesses, one must ask what protection remains for local families and farmers when those witnesses are no longer present,” Fawadleh said. “No individual should have to risk physical assault simply to harvest olives from their own land.” On Friday, Israeli militants attacked and severely injured Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine as she reported on the harvest in the town of Abu Falah. She required surgery on Saturday morning and is now in “moderate” condition, according to a spokesperson for Israel’s Beilinson hospital where she is being treated. Israel had already severely restricted the harvest this year by imposing new rules barring Palestinians from trees located in Area C, an area under the Israeli military’s control, which comprises most of the West Bank’s agricultural land. Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, condemned the attacks and said police had opened an investigation. He said foreign diplomats risked attacks from Israeli civilians if they travelled in the occupied West Bank without military coordination. Demanding diplomats give advance notification of travel violates both diplomatic conventions international law, said one western diplomatic source who asked not to be named. “Israel is in charge of security in Area B and C (the majority of the West Bank), so is obliged to assure safety there for all,” the source said. A culture of near total impunity for Israeli violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has prompted former prime minister Ehud Olmert to call for the international criminal court to intervene. Gadi Eisenkot, an opposition politician and former general hoping to unseat prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu in elections held later this month described the attack as “Jewish terror under the auspices of the Israeli government”. Eisenkot backs Jewish Israeli expansion in occupied Palestine but wants militant violence brought under control because the attackers are “harming the settlement enterprise in [the West Bank] and national security”.
